FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Handloom and Khadi Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. This standard was first published in 1967. This standard has been revised encountered by the khadi industry in implementation of the standard. Following are the important changes carried out while revising this standard: of India under Trade and to overcome difficulties

a) Tolerances on length and width as notified by the Government Merchandise Marks Act, 1958 ( 43 of 1958 ) have been adopted.

b) For checking the conformity of the cloth to the requirements laid down in the standard, a provision has been made for testing of the samples in prevailing atmospheric conditions. However, in case of dispute, the samples shall be tested after conditioning in the standard atmospheric conditions. c) The standard provides for agreement between permissible number of defects in the cloth. the buyer and the seller with respect to

TWILL, WOOL TEXTILES -CLOTH, DYED - SPECIFICATION KHADI,

( First Revision )
1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes constructional particulars and other requirements of cloth twill, wool kbadi, dyed. 1.2 This standard does not specify the appearance, feel, finish, etc, of the cloth. 2 REFERENCES The Indian Standards listed at Annex A are necessary adjuncts to this standard. 3 ATMOSPHERIC TESTING CONDITIONS FOR general 4.2.1 The cloth shall be woven in 2/2 twill weave. The woollen yarn used in the manufacture of cloth shall be hand-spun from 52s quality wool and free from admixture of non-wool fibres. The approximate count of warp and weft yam is given in Table 1. 4.2 Cloth

4.2.2 The cloth shall be clean, scoured, and free from grease, soap, filling or any other admixture which would give fictitious weight, substance or firmness to the cloth. 4.2.3 The cloth shall be dyed to shades to between the buyer and the seller. 4.2.4 The cloth shall have a milled as agreed

Test specimens may be conditioned and tested in the prevailing atmospheric conditions for checking the conformity of the cloth to the standard. However, in case of dispute, the specimens shall be conditioned and tested in the standard atmosphere as specified in the referred Indian Standards on test methods. 4 MANUFACTURE 4.1 Yarn

finish.

4.2.5 If required by the buyer, the cloth shall be mothproofed ( see IS 11662 : 1986 ). 5 REQUIREMENTS 5.1 Constructional particulars and breaking load of the cloth shall conform to the requirements specified in Table 1.

IS 4372 : 1994 5.2 The cloth shall also conform requirements specified in Table 2. 5.3 Dimensions Length and width of the cloth when determined in accordance with IS 1954 : 1990 shall be as agreed to between the buyer and the seller or as declared by the seller subject to the tolerances notified by the Government of India, Ministry of Commerce and Industry vide Notification No. S.O. 2937 dated 20 September 1962 issued under Trade andMerchandise Marks Act 1958 (43 of 1958) ( see Annex C ). 5.4 Freedom from Defects 6 MARKING 6.1 The cloth shall be suitably following information: marked with the to the other 5.5.2 The custody of the sealed sample shall be a matter of prior agreement between the buyer and the seller.

a) Name of the material; b) Length (m) and width (cm); and c) Indication of the source of manufacture. 6.2 BIS Certification Marking with the Standard

5.4.1 The cloth when visually inspected shall be as far as possible free from major flaws given in Annex D. However, the number of permissible flaws per unit length may be agreed to between the buyer and the seller. 5.4.2 For details of the flaws mentioned in 5.4.1, a reference may be made to IS 4125 : 1987. 5.5 Sealed Sample 5.5.1 In order to illustrate or specify the indeterminable characteristics, such as general appearance, feel and shade, if a sample has been agreed upon and sealed, the supply shall also be in conformity with the sample in such respects. The cloth may also be marked Mark.

6.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which licence for the use of the Standard Mark may he granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 7 PACKING Unless otherwise agreed upon by the buyer and the seller, the cloth shall preferably be packed in bales or cases in conformity with the procedure laid down in IS 32 : 1971 or IS 741 : 1971. B

( Table 1 )
METHOD FOR DETERMINATION OF MASS OF FABRIC mass in weighing balance

B-l Cut four specimens of 100 mm x 100 mm from a sample. Condition all the specimens in the desiccator charged with saturated solution of sodium nitrate at 27 + 2OC for a period of 24 hours. Remove all the specimens from the desiccator and immediately

determine their collective to the nearest milligram.

B-2 Calculate

mass of fabric

in g/m".

ANNEX

C

( Clause 5.3 )
EXTRACTS FROM THE AND INDUSTRY ( TRADE GOVERNMENT OF INDIA, MINISTRY OF AND MECHANISED MARRS ) NOTIFICATION 2937, DATED 20 SEFl-EMBER 1962 COMMERCE NO. S.O.

1. A trade description of length stamped on worsted, woollen and shoddy piece goods, the actual length of the piece shall not be less than stamped length. 2. A trade description of width stamped on worsted, woollen and shoddy piece goods: i) in pieces of worsted fabric, the stamped width shall not be greater or less than the actual

width provided that the variation in width at any point is not more than 2 percent and on average not more than 1.5 percent. ii) in pieces of woollen and shoddy piece goods, the stamped width shall not be greater or less than the actual width provided that the variation in width at any point is not more than 3 percent and on average not more than 2 percent.
